newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains lower on profit taking, shipper trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains lower on profit taking, shipper trade.

text.p: LIFFE wheat ended an active day lower as market players took profits from this week's small bounce off lows, traders said.
The most active month was November, which last traded 0.50 stg down at 86.25 stg. November volume was 361 lots of a total 713 on wheat.
Front month July was out of the spotlight, with just 46 lots done. It last traded 0.50 stg lower at 86.25 stg.
Some fresh farmer selling contributed to new crop's fall but it was shipper to shipper selling on the new crop as some took profits which had the most impact on prices, one trader said.
Old crop came down as players moved to take profits from its recent limited rally and move into new crop, he said.

Barley trade was just 36 lots, 35 of them on November, which last traded 0.35 stg lower at 84.75 stg. The fall was a result of traders buying wheat and selling barley with a view to the spread widening, he said.
Physical market players complained about a shortage of offers. "Enough people want what's coming off farm to absorb it," one said.
Feed wheat was reported done for July at 85 stg for Norfolk/Suffolk delivery, while barley was done for June to Norfolk/Suffolk at 82 stg. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
